root_cause.text: The GRO/frag_list GSO fast path incorrectly trusted XLAT-translated skbs as fully consistent, because `bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6()` and `bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4()` changed only the head skb’s protocol/header but did not mark the skb as `SKB_GSO_DODGY`, allowing `skb_segment_list` to segment partially untranslated frag_list packets.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly adds `shinfo->gso_type |= SKB_GSO_DODGY;` in both XLAT helpers in `net/core/filter.c`, and updates `tcp4_gso_segment()`, `tcp6_gso_segment()`, and `__udp_gso_segment()` to bypass the frag_list fast path when `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is set, with the commit message stating that `skb_segment_list cannot correctly process GRO skbs that have been converted by XLAT, since XLAT only translates the header of the head skb`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark IPv4-to-IPv6 converted skbs as GSO-dodgy to prevent incorrect offload handling after protocol translation.
intent_record.what: In bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6(), after updating the skb shared info GSO type from TCPv4 to TCPv6 inside the existing conditional block, the code now also sets the SKB_GSO_DODGY flag on shinfo->gso_type.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets converted from IPv4 to IPv6 are now marked as potentially unsafe for normal GSO assumptions, which can cause later networking code to treat the skb conservatively and avoid incorrect offload handling after the protocol change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark translated IPv6-to-IPv4 GSO packets as dodgy to ensure correct handling after protocol conversion.
intent_record.what: In `bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4(struct sk_buff *skb)`, a new line was added inside the existing GSO-handling block to set `shinfo->gso_type |= SKB_GSO_DODGY;` after the code that converts `SKB_GSO_TCPV6` to `SKB_GSO_TCPV4`.
intent_record.how: When an skb is rewritten from IPv6 to IPv4, the packet is now explicitly marked as potentially unsafe or needing special GSO handling. This changes runtime behavior by preventing the stack from treating the converted offload metadata as fully trusted after protocol translation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid using the FRAGLIST GSO fast path for DODGY skbs by requiring a non-dodgy GSO type before list segmentation.
intent_record.what: In tcp4_gso_segment(), the existing FRAGLIST fast-path condition was expanded by adding an extra check: the code now only calls __tcp4_gso_segment_list(skb, features) when the payload-length equality test succeeds and SKB_GSO_DODGY is not set in skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets marked as DODGY will no longer take the FRAGLIST segmentation shortcut even if their lengths match the expected GSO size. Instead, they fall through to the slower fallback path, which avoids treating potentially unreliable GSO metadata as valid for list-based segmentation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid use of the UDP fraglist GSO fast path when the skb is marked DODGY, forcing safer fallback segmentation.
intent_record.what: The fraglist fast path condition in __udp_gso_segment() was changed from checking only whether skb_pagelen(gso_skb) - sizeof(*uh) equals gso_size to additionally requiring that SKB_GSO_DODGY is not set in gso_type before calling __udp_gso_segment_list().
intent_record.how: At runtime, UDP GSO segmentation will no longer use the fraglist-based segmentation shortcut for skbs marked as DODGY, even if their page length matches the expected geometry; those packets will instead fall through to linearization and the generic segmentation path, avoiding use of potentially unreliable geometry information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip fraglist TCPv6 GSO list segmentation for SKB_GSO_DODGY packets to avoid incorrect handling of untrusted skb metadata.
intent_record.what: In tcp6_gso_segment(), the condition that selects __tcp6_gso_segment_list() was extended. It still requires FRAGLIST GSO and the payload length to match gso_size, but now it also requires that SKB_GSO_DODGY is not set in skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type. The rest of the surrounding logic is unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, fraglist-based TCPv6 GSO segmentation will no longer use the fast list-segmentation path for packets marked as dodgy. Such packets will fall through to the slower/default handling path instead, avoiding use of the specialized segmentation path when the skb metadata is not trusted.
